feature_request: Project managers should be able to see the full history of engagement with a country before starting a new mission.

proposed_scope_in.item: Read-only 'Engagement History' tab on the existing Country record, listing existing Engagement records for that country in reverse-chronological order (date, type, linked Contact, linked Project/Mission, summary text), with server-side pagination.

Access to the history tab inherits the existing Country/Mission permission model: a user sees only the Engagement records they can already see today, with no new roles, flags, or per-country settings.

Pre-mission entry point: on the 'Create Mission' screen, once a country is selected, show a link/inline summary (total engagements, date of most recent engagement, count of currently active missions) that opens the S1 history view for that country. Purely informational; it does not block or gate mission creation.

Basic filters on the history view using existing fields only: date range, engagement type, and linked Project/Mission. No saved views and no free-text search beyond the existing summary field search, if already available.

Every Engagement shown displays its linked Contact's current name and role as stored, with a link to the Contact record. Contacts marked inactive or departed in the existing data are visibly labelled, using the existing status field only.

proposed_scope_out: Any new data entry by Regional Coordinators: no new required fields, tags, or 'mission relevance' flags on Engagements
New entities or tables (no separate 'History' or 'Briefing' object); the view is a query over existing Country, Contact, Mission, Project, and Engagement records
AI-generated summaries, scoring, or 'relationship health' indicators
Export to PDF/Word, printable briefing packs, or email digests
Backfill, cleanup, or migration of historical engagement data; v1 shows what exists as it exists
Mandatory acknowledgment or approval step before a mission can be started ('must review history' gate)
Per-record sensitivity or classification tagging and redaction beyond the existing access model
Cross-country or regional rollup views (for example, all engagements across a region)
Edit or annotation of engagement history from the history view; it is strictly read-only
Notifications or alerts when new engagements are logged for a country
Defining 'full' history to include sources outside the CRM (email, calendar, document stores)

assumptions.statement: 'Full history of engagement' means all Engagement records already stored in the CRM for that country (directly or via its contacts, projects, and missions), with no retention cutoff in v1. It does not include external systems.
assumptions.rationale: Reusing the existing Engagement entity means no new schema and no migration, so a small team can ship in one cycle. Showing exactly what the CRM holds avoids a data-ingestion project.

assumptions.statement: Project managers already have an existing CRM role and can reach Country records and the Create Mission screen. The feature is a new read view, not a new user type.
assumptions.rationale: Avoids building identity or role management. Reusing current navigation puts the history where PMs already work, so no training or workflow change is needed.

assumptions.statement: The existing Country/Mission access model is the authority on who may see which Engagement records, and any institutional sensitivity or classification of engagement content is already reflected in that model. Deciding whether any engagement types need stricter handling is a policy decision for humans, not part of this MVP.
assumptions.rationale: Inheriting permissions means no custom RBAC to build and no new classification scheme to invent. It also keeps the MVP from making security-clearance decisions that belong to the institution.

assumptions.statement: 'Before starting a new mission' means surfacing history at the point of mission creation (an easy, visible route), not enforcing that PMs read it.
assumptions.rationale: A soft entry point delivers the value for almost no cost. A mandatory gate would need approval logic and exception handling, which is expensive and would frustrate busy users.

assumptions.statement: Existing Engagement and Contact data is good enough for a first release: Engagements carry a date, type, and link to a Country; Contacts carry a status field. Gaps and inconsistencies in older data are accepted and shown as-is.
assumptions.rationale: Requiring Regional Coordinators to clean up or add fields would stall the release and rot over time. Showing what exists exposes data gaps naturally, and any clean-up can be prioritized later using real usage evidence.

success_criteria.criterion: For 100% of the ~100 member countries, the Engagement History tab loads the first page (up to 50 records) in under 3 seconds at the 95th percentile, including countries with 1,000 or more engagement records.

Permission test: in acceptance testing with at least 3 user profiles that have different Country/Mission access, 0 Engagement records are displayed to a user who cannot view that record elsewhere in the CRM.

Within 60 days of release, at least 60% of new missions created have a history-view open for the same country by the creating user within the prior 24 hours, as measured from existing access logs or click events.
Zero new required fields are added to Engagement, Contact, Mission, Project, or Country forms, verified by comparing schema and form definitions before and after release.
Filtering by date range, type, or linked Project/Mission returns correct results in 100% of a test set of at least 20 filter combinations, and each filtered view returns within 3 seconds at p95.
100% of Engagements linked to a Contact whose existing status is inactive or departed display a visible status label in the history view, verified against a test set of at least 20 such records.

challenges.challenge_text: The existing Country/Mission permission model was built for the current record-level views, not for a PM browsing years of cross-mission history on a country. A PM scoped to Mission X in Country Y who opens the Country-level history tab may see engagements from other missions or projects, including notes about sensitive ministry meetings, simply because Country access exists. The acceptance test uses 3 profiles and checks only 'visible elsewhere', which could pass while the new aggregate view still exposes content that was previously hard to reach. S1 also pulls engagements 'directly or via contacts, projects, and missions', so an Engagement linked to a Contact in a mission the PM cannot access might leak through the contact link. Required: the query must apply the per-record mission and project scope filter, not only a country-level check. The test must include a PM with access to one mission in a country and confirm other missions' engagements are absent.
challenges.evaluation_of_proposer: Round 1; the Proposer asserts inheritance is sufficient and defers sensitivity decisions to humans, but has not shown that the model enforces mission-level scoping at the Engagement record level.

challenges.challenge_text: 'Full history with no retention cutoff' means a PM starting a new mission sees summary text and linked contacts from many years ago, including former ministers and staff, authored by long-departed coordinators. Old free-text summaries may hold candid assessments of individuals, or information shared under a past administration, that were never meant for wide re-reading. S1 also exposes the full summary text by default, which is the most confidential field. Required: show summary text in a truncated or expand-on-click form, and log access to the history view per user and country so a leak or misuse can be investigated. Without access logging, nobody can tell who read a country's history after an incident.
challenges.evaluation_of_proposer: Round 1; no defense yet. The Proposer treats retention as out of scope but does not bound the exposure of free text summaries.

challenges.challenge_text: S5 displays each Engagement's linked Contact's current name and role, as stored. Contacts turn over constantly across 100 countries. A 2019 engagement with the then Minister of Trade will show whoever now occupies that Contact record or its stale role, or a contact flagged active that has actually left. A PM may then call or email the wrong person at the ministry, or believe the relationship is still live. Only the status field is labelled, and A5 accepts that it is likely stale or blank. Required: show the Contact's name and role as of the engagement date if captured, or at least a 'last verified' date on the contact, and treat a blank or unknown status as an explicit 'status unknown' label rather than showing nothing. Otherwise the 100% label criterion only covers records already marked correctly.
challenges.evaluation_of_proposer: Round 1; the Proposer accepts stale data as-is, which makes the history view appear authoritative while silently misleading.

challenges.challenge_text: S3 shows 'count of currently active missions' and the most recent engagement date on the Create Mission screen. If this count includes missions the PM cannot access, it leaks the existence of confidential missions in a country. The summary figures may also be computed before permission filtering, so total engagements could differ from what the tab lists, confusing users and revealing hidden records. A sparse or stale 'most recent engagement' date may also mislead a PM into thinking a country is dormant when contacts simply were not logged. Required: compute all summary counts after the same permission filter as S1, and label them 'visible to you'.
challenges.evaluation_of_proposer: Round 1; no defense yet. Summary aggregates are not covered by the S2 permission test.

challenges.challenge_text: The Proposer assumes the PM role already exists and can reach every Country record. In practice PMs may hold broad roles or be assigned countries loosely, and a new mission creator will often select a country they have no prior access to, which is the very moment they want history. Either the PM sees nothing, which defeats the feature, or someone widens access to make it work, which breaks least-privilege. The 60% usage metric also cannot distinguish these cases. Required: define the behavior when a PM selects a country they lack access to, such as a clear 'no access, request via coordinator' message that reveals no counts, and verify the PM role's current Country access in the existing data before release.
challenges.evaluation_of_proposer: Round 1; the Proposer treats the role assumption as settled without evidence on real access scope.

challenge_responses.response: The risk is real and the fix is cheap: it is a rule on the query, not new schema. S2 now requires the per-record Engagement-level Mission/Project check used by existing Engagement views, with no visibility granted by Country access or by a Contact link alone. The acceptance test now includes a PM with access to one mission in a multi-mission country and asserts that other missions' Engagements are absent, including those reachable only via Contact. If the existing model turns out not to enforce mission-level scoping at Engagement level, widening or redefining it is a security-authority decision for humans, and I would escalate it rather than invent a rule.

Two cheap changes are adopted: summary text is truncated to 200 characters with expand-on-click, and opening the tab writes one entry (user, country, timestamp) to the existing access/audit log. No new table, dashboard, or review queue. We defend the absence of a retention cutoff and redaction: deciding what old content is too sensitive to re-read is institutional data-classification policy, not product design, so it is flagged for human decision. Since views are permission-filtered per C1 and now logged, the residual exposure is bounded and investigable. Evidence to revisit later: incident reports or a policy ruling on engagement-age cutoffs.

Partly adopted. Cheap: blank or unknown status is now labelled 'status unknown', the Contact's existing system 'record last updated' date is shown, and a fixed note states that name and role are current, not as of the engagement date. This removes the silent-authority problem at no data-entry cost. Defended: as-of-engagement-date name and role would need historical snapshots (a new table or per-engagement copy), and a coordinator-maintained 'last verified' field would violate the zero-data-entry goal and rot. Both are out of scope. Residual risk is a PM contacting a stale person; the note and update date bound it. Revisit if usage shows PMs acting on stale contacts.

Agreed and cheap: S3 figures now come from the same permission-filtered query as S1, so they cannot reveal hidden missions or records, and they are labelled 'visible to you'. The 'most recent engagement' date is labelled 'most recent logged' to avoid implying dormancy. A new criterion checks that S3 summaries equal the S1 totals for every test profile, closing the gap that the S2 test did not cover aggregates.

Adopted the cheap parts. S3 now defines what happens when a PM selects a country they cannot access: a fixed 'no access - request via your Regional Coordinator' message with no counts, dates, or mission numbers. A one-time pre-release query documents what Country access the PM role has today, recorded as a release check. We defend not widening access to make the feature work: whether PMs should get broader Country access is a security/authority decision for humans and is not made here. If the check shows PMs commonly lack access at mission creation, that goes to humans as a policy question.

final_decision.feature_request: Project managers should be able to see the full history of engagement with a country before starting a new mission.
final_decision.executive_summary: Version 1 adds a read-only Engagement History tab to the Country record and an informational summary on the Create Mission screen. Both show only the Engagements the user can already see, filtered per record by Mission/Project access. The tab lists existing Engagement records with 200-character summary truncation, basic filters, Contact status labels, and one access-log entry for each open. The main trade-off was exposure and data staleness against zero new data entry and no new schema. The Critic's five challenges (C1-C5) were each answered with cheap query, display, and logging changes and ended ACCEPTED in round 2. No scope is pending and no issue was escalated, so no human decision is currently required for this release.

Point-in-time (as-of-engagement-date) snapshots of Contact name and role, and any coordinator-maintained 'last verified' field
A dashboard, report, or review queue for the access log; the log is write-only in v1 and is consulted only during incident investigation
Retention cutoffs or redaction of old engagement summaries (a human policy decision)
success_criteria: For 100% of the ~100 member countries, the Engagement History tab loads the first page (up to 50 records) in under 3 seconds at the 95th percentile, including countries with 1,000 or more engagement records. (measures S1)

Permission test: in acceptance testing with at least 4 user profiles, including a PM with access to only one Mission in a multi-mission country, 0 Engagement records are displayed that the user cannot view elsewhere in the CRM, and 0 Engagements from the other missions or projects appear for the single-mission PM, including Engagements reachable only via a Contact link. (measures S2, S1)

Summary consistency test: for every test profile, the S3 engagement count and most-recent date equal the total and top row of the S1 tab for that same user, and the active-mission count includes only missions the user can access (0 discrepancies). (measures S3, S2)

No-access test: for a user without access to a selected country, the Create Mission screen shows the no-access message and 0 counts, dates, or mission numbers in 100% of at least 5 test cases. (measures S3)

Within 60 days of release, at least 60% of new missions created have a history-view open for the same country by the creating user within the prior 24 hours, as measured from the existing access log. (measures S3, S1)

Summary text longer than 200 characters is truncated with an expand control in 100% of tested records, and 100% of history-tab opens in testing produce exactly one access-log entry with user, country, and timestamp. (measures S1)
Zero new required fields are added to Engagement, Contact, Mission, Project, or Country forms, verified by comparing schema and form definitions before and after release. (measures S1, S3, S4, S5)

Filtering by date range, type, or linked Project/Mission returns correct results in 100% of a test set of at least 20 filter combinations, and each filtered view returns within 3 seconds at p95. (measures S4)

100% of Engagements linked to a Contact whose existing status is inactive, departed, or blank display a visible label ('inactive', 'departed', or 'status unknown') in the history view, verified against a test set of at least 20 such records, and every Contact shows its record-last-updated date. (measures S5)
Pre-release check: before launch, a one-time query documents which Countries the PM role can currently access and the result is recorded; no access rule is widened for this release. (measures S3, S2)

surfaced_assumptions.assumption: 'Full history of engagement' means all Engagement records already stored in the CRM for that country (directly or via its contacts, projects, and missions), with no retention cutoff in v1. It does not include external systems.
surfaced_assumptions.resolution_notes: C2 challenged the no-retention-cutoff history and exposed summary text. It ended ACCEPTED after the Proposer added 200-character truncation with expand-on-click and access logging, and left retention cutoffs out of scope.

surfaced_assumptions.assumption: Project managers already have an existing CRM role and can reach Country records and the Create Mission screen. The feature is a new read view, not a new user type.
surfaced_assumptions.resolution_notes: C5 challenged whether PMs can reach every Country. It ended ACCEPTED after the Proposer defined a no-access message with no counts and added a one-time pre-release check of PM Country access, with no access widened.

surfaced_assumptions.assumption: The existing Country/Mission access model is the authority on who may see which Engagement records, and any institutional sensitivity or classification of engagement content is already reflected in that model. Deciding whether any engagement types need stricter handling is a policy decision for humans, not part of this MVP.
surfaced_assumptions.resolution_notes: C1 challenged whether the existing permission model protects an aggregate history view. It ended ACCEPTED after S2 was revised to filter per record by Mission/Project access and the tests added a single-mission PM.

surfaced_assumptions.assumption: 'Before starting a new mission' means surfacing history at the point of mission creation (an easy, visible route), not enforcing that PMs read it.
surfaced_assumptions.resolution_notes: C4 challenged the Create Mission summary figures leaking hidden records or implying a dormant country. It ended ACCEPTED after the figures were computed after the permission filter, labelled 'visible to you', and covered by a consistency test.

surfaced_assumptions.assumption: Existing Engagement and Contact data is good enough for a first release: Engagements carry a date, type, and link to a Country; Contacts carry a status field. Gaps and inconsistencies in older data are accepted and shown as-is.
surfaced_assumptions.resolution_notes: C3 challenged stale or blank Contact data. It ended ACCEPTED after the Proposer added a 'status unknown' label, the Contact's last-updated date, and a fixed note that details are current. Point-in-time snapshots and a 'last verified' field were left out of scope.
